sources.author: Swyx
sources.headline: AI Engineer | Founder @ Latent Space | Building the AI Engineer community
sources.post_summary: Dropped a detailed breakdown of how Claude's extended thinking mode is changing the economics of agentic pipelines. When you can bill for reasoning tokens separately, the cost-per-correct-output math inverts — suddenly long-horizon tasks that felt too expensive become the cheapest path. This is the sleeper shift nobody's pricing into their infra decisions.

sources.author: Lenny Bogdonoff
sources.headline: Staff Engineer @ Anthropic | Previously: OpenAI | Building tools for AI builders
sources.post_summary: We quietly shipped multi-agent handoff with full memory carry-over last week and the internal adoption curve is vertical. The pattern that works: treat context as a first-class artifact, not an afterthought. Every agent hand-off is a structured document, not a summary. Teams that got this right cut debugging time by 60%.

sources.author: Alessio Fanelli
sources.headline: Partner @ Decibel Ventures | Co-host @ Latent Space Podcast | Investing in AI-native dev tools
sources.post_summary: Five AI dev tool startups I talked to this week all said the same thing: their biggest competitor is Claude Code, not each other. This is what platform risk looks like in real time — not a slow squeeze but a fast collapse of the mid-market. The winners will be the ones who build on top of the wave, not beside it.

sources.author: Hamel Husain
sources.headline: Independent AI Consultant | Ex-GitHub, Hugging Face | Helping companies actually ship AI products
sources.post_summary: Controversial take: most 'AI agent' demos are just API chaining with a for-loop. Real agents need three things you almost never see in a demo — durable state, graceful degradation, and an eject hatch for humans. Until eval frameworks catch up to these requirements, we're measuring the wrong things and shipping the wrong things.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: CMO at Clari | Revenue Intelligence | GTM Strategy
sources.post_summary: We cut our SDR team by 40% and grew pipeline by 60%. The secret: we stopped using reps for research and qualification and built an AI-first outbound engine instead. Here's the exact stack and workflow we shipped in 6 weeks.

sources.author: Tamara Gielen
sources.headline: VP Revenue Operations @ Series B SaaS | RevOps Systems | GTM Alignment
sources.post_summary: Your CRM is lying to you. After auditing 12 RevOps orgs this year, the #1 problem isn't bad data — it's that no one owns the definition of 'qualified.' Every team has a different answer. Here's the single-source-of-truth doc we use to fix it.

sources.author: Jason Vargas
sources.headline: Head of Growth Engineering | Clay, Apollo, AI Outbound | B2B GTM
sources.post_summary: I built a Clay → Apollo → Smartlead waterfall that auto-researches 500 accounts a day, writes personalized first lines from their job posts, and books 3x more meetings than our old spray-and-pray sequences. Full breakdown with the exact tables and prompts in the comments.

sources.author: Lara Vandenberg
sources.headline: Content Strategy → Pipeline | B2B SaaS | Dark funnel & demand gen
sources.post_summary: Most B2B content teams are optimizing for impressions. The teams winning in 2026 are optimizing for reactivation — content that gets forwarded to buying committees. I mapped our last 8 closed-won deals back to which specific posts they shared internally. The results were not what I expected.

sources.author: Maya Krishnamurthy
sources.headline: Solo founder | Built and sold my first SaaS | Now building #2 in public
sources.post_summary: Maya shipped her second product in 47 days using Claude Code and Cursor, documenting every build session on LinkedIn. She broke down her MRR progression week by week ($0 → $3,200) and shared the exact moment she realized she'd priced too low. The post resonated because she included the rejection screenshots alongside the wins.

sources.author: Derek Osei
sources.headline: Ex-accountant → developer | 14 months of learning | Shipped my first paid product last week
sources.post_summary: Derek posted a side-by-side of his first messy Python script from 14 months ago versus the Go API he shipped to paying customers last Tuesday. He was brutally honest about the 6-month plateau where he almost quit, and what finally clicked. Career pivoters flooded the comments with their own timelines.

sources.author: Priya Nambiar
sources.headline: GTM engineer | Replacing $40k/yr tools with $200/mo AI agents | Writing about it
sources.post_summary: Priya documented how she replaced her company's entire outbound stack with three Claude agents she built over a weekend, cutting tooling costs from $3,800/mo to $180/mo. She included the actual system prompts, the failure modes she hit, and why most people building AI agents are over-engineering them. Post spread fast in RevOps and GTM circles.

sources.author: Tom Callahan
sources.headline: Shipping one micro-SaaS per month | 0 VC | 100% bootstrapped
sources.post_summary: Tom posted a raw retrospective after month 6 of his shipping streak — three products dead, two still alive, one generating $890/mo passively. He shared his exact validation checklist that he now runs before writing a single line of code, and admitted the two survivors came from scratching his own itches rather than 'finding a market.' The comment section turned into a masterclass on micro-SaaS positioning.
